title: A faithfully flat ring epimorphism is an isomorphism
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with identity and $f:R\to S$ a unital ring homomorphism. Assume $f$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Assume also that it is an epimorphism of commutative rings: for every commutative ring $B$ and unital ring homomorphisms $a,b:S\to B$, if $a\circ f=b\circ f$ then $a=b$. Then $f$ is bijective, and hence an isomorphism of rings. No finite-generation or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04VU, lemma-faithfully-flat-epimorphism (statement and proof), the general ring-theoretic result invoked by the proof of Tag 04VV in the inherited Tag 03DP/direct-image ancestry.

proof.text: Give $S$ its $R$-algebra structure through $f$ and form $T=S\otimes_R S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], the maps $i_1,i_2:S\to T$ given by $i_1(s)=s\otimes1$ and $i_2(s)=1\otimes s$ are unital $R$-algebra homomorphisms. Thus $i_1f=i_2f$ (both send $r$ to $f(r)\otimes1=1\otimes f(r)$). Apply precisely the assumed epimorphism property with the commutative ring $B=T$ to obtain $i_1=i_2$.

source.place: Tag 04VU, lemma-faithfully-flat-epimorphism, proof invoking lemma-epimorphism (2); the omitted implication (1) to (2) is expanded here.

proof.text: The multiplication homomorphism $\mu:T\to S$, $\mu(s\otimes t)=st$, is the map in clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] for the two identity maps of $S$. We have $\mu i_1=\mathrm{id}_S$. On a pure tensor, the equality $i_1=i_2$ from step 1 gives $i_1\mu(s\otimes t)=st\otimes1=(s\otimes1)(t\otimes1)=(s\otimes1)(1\otimes t)=s\otimes t$. Since pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $i_1\mu=\mathrm{id}_T$. Hence $i_1$ and $\mu$ are mutually inverse.

source.place: Tag 04VU, lemma-faithfully-flat-epimorphism, proof invoking lemma-epimorphism (3); the omitted tensor-product inverse calculation is expanded here.

proof.text: Tensor the $R$-linear map $f:R\to S$ on the left with $S$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $u:S\otimes_R R\to S$, $u(s\otimes r)=sf(r)$, with inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$: balancing gives $sf(r)\otimes1=s\otimes r$. The tensor map $S\otimes_R f$ sends $s\otimes r$ to $s\otimes f(r)=sf(r)\otimes1$, so equals $i_1u$ and is bijective by step 2. Also $S\otimes_R0=0$, since pure tensors with a zero entry vanish and generate. The complexes $0\to R\xrightarrow{f}S$ and $R\xrightarrow{f}S\to0$ therefore become exact after tensoring with $S$. Apply the exactness-reflection clause of the very definition [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] to each complex: $\ker f=0$ and $\operatorname{im}f=S$. Thus $f$ is bijective. Its inverse preserves addition, multiplication and $1$, by applying the injective map $f$ to each required equality; hence $f$ is a ring isomorphism.
